notes: (1) The exemption is keyed on the record's self-declared 'experiment' field. A record written or hand-edited as experiment E1/E2/E3 skips the required-metric check, and nothing requires the run_id/file-name prefix to equal the experiment (own6.py: E9 file edited to experiment 'E1' passes 'check_run E9'). This needs deliberate falsification of a self-declared field, like dirty or git_commit, so I did not count it as a failure; cheap hardening would be requiring run_id to start with the experiment name, or exempting by run_id/commit. (2) The WinError 6 explanation could not be checked from a written record; a real training run with num_workers>0 under heavy load could in principle hit a worker handle failure, and recovery would be an explicit resume from the atomically written last checkpoint (same settings, num_workers may differ), which the code supports. (3) E3 is exempt by name until its figures are added to topk-baselines.json after T3.3. Scratch files are in orchestration/evidence/tmp-T3.5/ (own4.py, own5.py, own6.py). Nothing was written to the real results/runs/.
